English: The Crimean War
Once again, the negotiations with the Byzantine Empire have broken down, and we are left with no choice but to seize Crimea by force. To arms!
Reclaim the Frontier

During the Great Peninsular War of 1756-1777, the combined Leonese-Occitan armies have overwhelmed the forces of Al-Andalus and pushed us behind the Tagus river. Now, the time has come to cross the wretched river and liberate the Muslims under Spanish rule!
Trapezuntine Tea

Despite the growing popularity of tea in $COUNTRY$, there are no tea producing provinces in our homeland. Now the microclimate region along the eastern coast of the Black Sea was identified by specialists as an ideal spot to start tea production, which will contribute to the task of fulfilling the growing demand for tea by the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ citizens.
Diplomacy has failed.
Develop Klyuchevsk

Klyuchevsk, meaning "key town" in Russian, was founded on the Baltic Coast in 1732 in place of the old fortress of Oreshek. It was intended to be the primary Russian port on the Baltic, however, the marshes around the river Neva turned out to be too costly to drain, so the construction was subsequently abandoned and the town remained relatively small. Now, however, we have the necessary technologies to finally bring the city to its intended glory.
Unite the Yue

Our Northern neighbours are finally waking up from their slumber. This means that things cannot continue the way they are right now: the division between Nanyue and Minyue must end. We must unify the Yue and create a prosperous realm in the South!
Integrate Taiwan

When the Ming dynasty fell, the island of Taiwan was seized by imperial loyalists, who established the Tungning kingdom with Koxinga in charge. We have since ignored the island, being content with a simple poorly-enforced blockade on these morons with delusional ideas of 'imperial restoration'. Things are much different now, and we must finally end the status quo and properly integrate the valuable island into our realm.
Hegemony in Annam

The Kingdom of Nanyue of old held the entirety of modern Tonkin and Annam, enjoying the hegemony over the Gulf of Tonkin and the lucrative trade here. With the Dainamese people being quite culturally similar to us, we can finally finish what was started almost a century ago and incorporate the Nguyen kingdom into our realm.
Formalize Southern Borders

Having secured the loyalty of the Dainamese, we may now turn our attention to securing the flanks of our newly-conquered lands. The opportunistic Lao tribes, despite being pushed back significantly, still hold the high ground over Tonkin, and the Dali kings rule over a large amount of Zhuang peoples, who would much rather stay with us.
Northern Expedition

Ever since the Han Empire conquered Nanyue and Minyue in the 2nd century BC, the South has been in a subservient position to the emperors of the North. We finally rid ourselves of this status when we broke off from the Shun in the 17th century, and now it is time for the Yue to show the Han that we are a force to be reckoned with. We shall organize a grand expedition to the North and seize the borderlands, where the local Hakka population will surely welcome us.
Liberate the Wu

Out of all of the Southern peoples, the Wu have had the weakest national identity of all. Located in lands firmly held by the Shun, who suppressed any notion of distinct national identity, the Wu are mostly content with the current flow of things. We, however, know better: securing at least the southern part of Anhui will bring a significant amount of loyal peoples under our rule and put the major Han city of Nanjing into a vulnerable position, making the Han think twice before attempting to reclaim these lands.
Reinforce Bo-Ni

The island of Bo-Ni, known to the locals as Kalimantan and to the Westerners as Borneo, houses a significant amount of Chinese immigrants, who came here to work for the kongsi, which are mining organizations that exploit the local gold and tin depostits. They are the primary reason for why we currently hold lands on the island, and we see no reason not to expand their operations over the rest of the island, considering the activization of European activities in the area.
Proclaim the South China Sea Hegemony

The South China Sea has been a traditional area of operations for the Min and the Yue, where we conducted our trade and held much influence. As such, it is logical that our primary objective should be establishing total control over the coastal areas of the sea, annexing large swathes of land that are currently held by the imperialist powers of the West. They surely won't be too happy about our ambitions, but who are they to stop the rising Yue thalassocracy?
Accept the Tawalisi
The people of the Tawalisi archipelago have historically maintained close ties with our merchants. Now that we are in control of the islands, we may integrate them into our society for good.
Accept the Minor Peoples

Our goal of hegemony in the South China Sea made us come into closer contact with several less significant peoples of Southeast Asia, such as the Cham. Having been oppressed by their overlords, most of them think of us as of another conqueror. We must prove them wrong and secure their loyalty, as they will be a useful asset in further strengthening of our country.
Unify China

China lies in a sorry state. Petty lords wage war for land, barbarians besiege the realm and the Imperial authority is non-existent. By crushing all opposition and enforcing our will all over China, we may finally put an end to the internal strife and unify the Middle Kingdom under our banner.
Reclaim the South

During the collapse of the Ming Dynasty, the Southern coast of China was seized by the merchant states of Nanyue and Minyue, who since have established their own distinct national identities. This cannot continue, we must do what Shun failed to do two hundred years ago - bring them back into the fold!
Reclaim Yunnan

The Kingdom of Dali is a relatively new polity, being established during the hasty retreat of the Shun. The largely Muslim kingdom must be annexed into China, no matter whether they think of themselves as a neutral country.
Enact Freedom of Religion

With each passing year we feel more pressure both from within and from the outside to get on with the times and accept the large amount of Muslims in our country. With the recent changes to our political landscape, we can finally recognize the Hui as equals.
Integrate the South

The destruction of independent polities in the South means that we can finally begin the process of reintegration of the local population into the economic and political life of our country. The centuries of cultivated hatred towards the Han has certainly had its effect, and no matter what the process will be quite arduous and time-consuming.
Reclaim Taiwan

In the 17th century, a large amount of Ming loyalists together with their leader Koxinga have fled to the island of Taiwan, establishing their own kingdom with the goal of reclaiming the mainland. Times are surely different now, and no matter the political landscape on the island, the valuable island must be brought into the fold, for the first time ever.
The Northern Frontier

No Chinese Empire has exerted full control over the Gobi desert, which served as a natural protection against the nomads of Mongolia. However, it is becoming increasingly clear that the important cities of the North, such as Beijing, can only be sufficiently guarded if we control the desert and the Manchurian coast ourselves. Besides, the land is rich with natural resources, which we will make sure to use during our industrialization.
The $CAPITAL$ Arsenal

With the proliferation of Western firearms, we are starting to feel the difficulties of actually buying them from the Europeans. Either raising the prices to an unreasonable value, or outright refusing to sell anything to us, the Europeans are unreliable. We must establish local production of modern weapons in our capital.
The Korean Candidate

The peoples of China and Korea have historically been very close, their history and culture intertwined inseparably. A most ambitious plan proposed by King Munjo promises to elevate this connection to a highest level, and if our expedition into China succeeds, this may very well erase all divisions between the Han of China and the Han of Korea.
Conquer Manchuria

The Conquest of Manchuria technically started in th 17th century, when the fall of the Ming prompted Korea to begin undertaking active measures to ensure its safety. However, we've never managed to properly subjugate most of the Wild Jurchens, as well as the Korchin Mongols and the Evenks residing North of the Amur river. Now it is time to right this wrong and finish what we started two centuries ago.
Annex Hwang'tae

The island of Hwang'tae, known to the Japanese as Karafuto and to the Russians as Sakhalin, lies right at the coast of our posessions in Manchuria. Controlling it would ensure safety of the Tatar Strait, though at the cost of angering the Russians and possibly dragging us into a future conflict with the Japanese.
An End to Chaos

One of the primary reasons of our current invasion is to secure peace and stability in East Asia, which has been plagued by chaos for nearly a century. The North might have been pacified, but the South remains unruly and chaotic. It is time to end the warlords once and for all!
China United

The pacification of China has been successful. The warlords are no more, the foreign enroachers are crushed beneath our armies. It is time to properly integrate the Chinese bureaucracy and fix the consequences of decades of civil strife.
Middle Kingdoms Intervention

After a long period of dormancy, things have finally kicked off in China. The small warlord statelets to the East are embroiled in bloody conflicts, trying to gain the upper hand in the process of Chinese Reunification. And it just so happens to be that the weakest of these states, Qin, sits right at our border. Perhaps, this opportunity might turn into something bigger... \n§RYou need to have 4 times more brigades than the owner of Shensi.
Into the Chaos

The Kingdom of Qin fell before our armies, their bureaucracy being integrated into ours. This means that we are ready to advance to the next step of our great plan: the crossing of the mountains to the South and the invasion of the fertile plains of Yangtze.
The Open Plains

We have advanced deep into Chinese territory, now entering the so-called 'Central Plain'. This means that our cavalry can roam free all across the most important regions of China - we must exploit it to the fullest! \n§RUnlocks the Chinese Reunification CB.
Found the Xie Dynasty

The Han have considered the peoples of the steppes to be their biggest enemy, even building the Great Wall to keep us out of China. Alas, this did not help them, as we are now at the brink of unifying China. It seems like in their pride they have forgotten the Buddhist principles many of them claim to follow, and so we shall bring the word of Dalai Lama to them and found an empire where there is no place for hate - the Xie Empire!
Liberate Manchuria

The Manchus are close relatives of the Mongols, but despite that, they never really acomplished anything of note besides the establishment of the short-lived Jin dynasty. Currently they are being colonized by the Koreans and the Russians, and, as a brotherly steppe-dwelling nation, we shall liberate them and add them into the fray.
Begin the Southern Reclamation
With the Northern Capital in our hands, we may finally look to the South and crush the disorganized warlords that hold our rightful land. \n§RUnlocks the Chinese Reunification CB.
Reclaim Ayutthaya
Once we gather enough strength, we may finally challenge the Burmese occupiers and reclaim the ancestal lands of the Thai, pressing our claim to estore a unified Siam, unseen since 1767.
Integrate Assam

Our unexpected victories in Assam have brought the local population, who hail us as liberators, to recognize our rule as legitimate in all of Assam. Let us embrace the Assamese, for they might prove to be a valuable asset against any Western threat.
End the Stagnation

The Konbaung Empire has been stagnant ever since the Sack of Ayutthaya in 1767, except for a few minor unseccessful engagements into Yunnan. This is a dangerous state of affairs, as we continue to rule over a large number of hostile peoples, whose desires for freedom are ever-increasing. We must rectify this and reform our kingdom to be a true regional hegemon, for if we do not do it now, the rising polities in the East that we failed to conquer may blow us a most humiliating blow.
Invade Malaya

The Malay Peninsula houses many small Muslim polities. They are disunited and weak, and yet their lands are rich and could provide control over the straits to the South. We must crush the, before the Europeans get to it.
Partition Cambodia

Several close advisors in our court have proposed offering a lucrative deal to our friends in France: partitioning the massive Cambodia between our countries. We could try to defeat them on our own, yes, bu we better now risk it and just take the opportunity we have, lest we might have a problem with the French interests in Cochinchina.
Annex Cambodia

Cambodia not only benefitted from the collapse of Ayutthaya, they also prevented the later unification and seized Thai-populated lands. Surely this is not the end of their ambitions, and we shall not allow them to become even mightier, like back in the days of the Khmer Empire. We need to crush them, even at a cost of potentially coming into conflicts with European interests in Cochinchina.
Annex Cambodia

The lands of Cambodia are populated by a nation closely related to our people - the Khmer. Their state no longer exists, and we must seize this opportunity and take the highly important heartland of the old Khmer Empire, lest it gets seized by Western imperialist powers.
Annex Laos
Our dominance in Laos is undisputed at this point. Let us properly finish the Lao and crush all resistance that might be left there.
Integrate Laos
With Laos annexed, we can start the process of integration of these unruly lands. Though it may be hard, it would be a major victory for the Thai state, for our old enemies are now our subjects.
Integrate Cambodia
Cambodia has been conquered by our triumphant armies. Let us integrate the local Khmer infrastructure and bureaucracy with our own, securing a highly-populated area for our growing kingdom.
Franco-Siamese Border Treaty

French Indoshina has grown beyond the wildest predictions of our colonial governors. We have successfully secured Dainam, and yet a certain issue bother us - the neighboring Siamese state, which controls many Lao lands and exerts substantial influence over Cambodia. We may just be able to persuade them into giving up their holdings in Laos, or, otherwise, take them by force.
Unite Indochina

The Indochinese Peninsula, as it is called by the Europeans, was never close to unification, as it is populated by diverse peoples, who more often than not held resentment for each other. The times are different, however, and the continued survival of our nation reqires a creation of a unified Indochinese identity.
Unite the Malay States

The small polities on the Malay Peninsula have never had a unified state of their own, instead each having its own prince. The time has come to end this state of affairs and unify the Malay states once and for all!
Reassert German Dominance

No doubt inspired by the revolution in Sweden, the Franconian Crisis was a dangerous precedent that cannot be allowed to happen again. It has shown that our current political course cannot guarantee safety for Germany and the German people, which means it is time to take a more active stance in our goal of German unification. \n§RUnlocks the German Unification CB
Form the South German Federation

The lands of Upper Germany have historically been closely intertwined with each other. The creation of the German Confederation moved the Kingdom of Bavaria and the constituents of the former Swabian Circle even closer together, and in our quest of German Unification, the creation of a unified Federation in the South would serve as an important step towards German Unity.
Three Hurrahs for Germany!

The idea of a unified Germany has been ever-present in the minds of the German people ever since the German Renaissance of the 1780s. The nation's efforts were directed entirely towards achieving that goal for more than 50 years, and despite many setbacks and defeats we've had to face, the German Dream still burns bright in our hearts. And no matter what, it shall triumph: The German Confederation shall finally cease to exist, instead giving way to a new power in Central Europe - the German Empire!
Retake Prussia

Prussia was unjustly stolen from us by the Zapadoslavs in the late 1830s, when Germany was shaken by the Franconian Crisis. They may tear Prussia away from the German Confederation, but they can't destroy the idea of a United Germany. The people of Prussia yearn for liberation, and let us deliver it!
Unite the Swiss

The Swiss population is currently divided between the Switzerland proper, a member of the Confederation, and the so-called 'Bern Confederation', a union of Western Swiss cities protected by the Arelat. It is no secret this political entity is entirely temporary, and now it is time to integrate the Confederation into the Greater German State.
Retake Schlesien

Silesia was once a part of the Holy Roman Empire, dominated by the Kingdom of Bohemia and being a place where the Slavic and the Germanic worlds met, the different peoples intermingling with each other. It ended with the secession of Bohemia from the Empire in 1716, and as they took Silesia with them, all German influence disappeared from the area. With the Unification of Germany we can turn our attention to the last remainders of Germans who are a sizeable minority in the area and press pur claim, however tenuous it might be.
The Western Reaches

As we finish the process of collecting all German lands under one state, we turn our attention to the weakest of our claims, those on the Western border. Here lie sizeable minorities and even majorities of Germans, most of them living in the part of Duchy of Luxemburg that was not included in the German Confederation, as well in the city of Metz and its surroundings. Taking these lands would be a boon to our prestige, and, most importantly, it will strengthen our position in any future conflicts in the area.
Venetian Autonomy

The rapidly changing situation in Italy threatens our posessions in Veneto, awarded to us during the Constantinople Accords. The local population, despite the relative distance of the old Venetian Republic from overall Italian politics, still considers itself Italian, and as such, they are becoming increasingly more hostile to us. Perhaps, if we were to create an autonomous Kingdom in these lands, we would be able to keep the tides of Italian nationalism at bay for the time being.
Form the North German Federation

Lower German states have not not played a significant role in German politics of the last centuries. Disunity accompanied us all the way since the conquest of these lands from the Slavic tribes, and we have utilized it how we could, the prime example being the Hanseatic League. The times are different now, and it is evident that we can no longer afford to be disunited. A Federation of all North German states will be the first step towards our idea of a unitary, centralised Germany.
Open the Frontiers

South Africa is a land of opportunity. The virgin prairies of Kaapland await those who are tired from war and poverty of Europe and want to start a new life. Lets us open the frontiers and welcome our brothers from across the pond!
Claim the Karoo

The Great Karoo desert houses many Trekboer nomads. While these lands are infertile, controlling would serve as great protection against any possible incursions from the north, however unlikely they will be.
The Northern Frontier

With the activization of European colonial activities in Africa comes the need to secure the lands we claimed in the North. We will establish outposts all over the lands we now call Namakwaland, thus firmly securing them for future settlement.
Along the Coast

The coast to our east houses a large population of Xhosa and Nguni peoples, with the latter being organized into the strongest state in the area, the Zulu Kingdom. This region has colloquially been known by the Europeans as Kaffraria, or, when referring to the Zulu part, Natalia. Securing the coast would mean securing the inner regions from European incursion.
Oranje-Vaal Campaign

With the coast secured, we may finally move into the lands known as Transvaal and Transorangia. There, several Boer republics have been established, though they are not big enough to play any role outside of the region. Lets us move into these lands and integrate our brethen.
The Push to Zambezi

Our expansion must not stop with the Bushveld. Several poorly-organized tribes exist in the north, on the banks of the great Zambezi River, and if we were to move quickly, we could potentially extend our border all the way to the River itself, thus solidifying our position as the hegemon of South Africa, and possibly even of the entire continent.
Absorb Catalonia

Across the Ebro River live the Catalan people. The have managed to stay independent for centuries due to being subjects under the mighty Occitan Kingdom, one of our greatest rivals. With the reconquest of the Frontier we may march into Barcelona once again, for the Occitans are no more and the united France has shown no interest in protecting their former subjects.
Reconquest of the East

The Long Peace of Iberia is coming to an end. The Moors are gearing up for the reclamation of their former lands, and the Catalan Republic is becoming increasingly unstable. Such circumstances force us to act, lest we will lose the initiative to our enemies. And the obvious direction of our actions would be to the East, where the people of the Ebro River toil under the Moorish thumb. We shall be welcomed as liberators - and it will only be the first step.
The Issue of Catalonia

Our swift push to the Mediterranean Sea has not gone unnoticed by the various political forces of the Catalan Republic. Many are saying that considering their diplomatic isolation, they will not be able to keep their independence. We must decide on our course of action.
Annex the Duchy of Barcelona

Time is out for the Dukes of Barcelona. They have enjoyed autonomy for several decades, but the circumstances are different now. For the continued prosperity of the realm, we must incorporate the lands of Catalonia directly into the Leonese state, ending their autonomy once and for all.
Press the Gothic Claim

Our decision to allow for a return of the Barcelona Dynasty offers us a unique opportunity. At different times, the Dukes of Barcelona were allowed to administer the March of Gothia, giving them a strong enough claim to the region. Pressing their claim would ruin our relations with the French, but it will grant us control over an important section of the Mediterranean coastline.
Reconquest of the Center

The Moorish hold on Iberia is weaker than ever following our liberation of the Ebro Valley and the Mediterranean coast. The balance of power in Iberia lies shattered, with the initiative in our hands. The centuries-long struggle to liberate the peoples of Iberia is finally coming to a close, for the inner Moorish lands are now our next target.
Finish the Reconquista

After more than a millenium, the Reconquista is coming to an end. The last strongholds of the Moors lie on the southern coast, known since Roman times as Baetica. Cordoba, Sevilla, Granada - all of these cities have been fully Arabized since times immemorial. We will finally take these lands and integrate them into Leon, for the betterment of all the peoples of Iberia.
Mauretanian Crusade

The lands of North Africa have once been Christian, but in the centuries following the rise of Islam almost all communities of the faithful have been wiped out. We have pushed the Moors to the Rock of Gibraltar, but the Reconquista is not quite over yet: we will chase them across the sea and eliminate any possibility of them threatening Iberia in the future.
Restore Al-Andalus

The Faithful have been pushed out of the Iberian Peninsula by the vile heathens of the north. If we manage to retake the heartlands of the Al-Andalus of old, we may proclaim the restoration of Muslim rule in Iberia.
Reverse Arabization

Centuries of Moorish rule in Iberia have had quite an impact on the ethnoreligious landscape of the lands. One of the most horrible things that the Moors have acomplished was an erasure of national identity and language, both of which have been adapted to fit into the greater Andalusi identity. With the consolidation of our rule in the South we can reverse this.
The Great Language Reform

Leon, and Iberia in general, is a land of great linguistical diversity. Many dialects and languages have developed independently of each other, and while it is fascinating for scholars, it is a nightmare for the bureaucrats. The strain that is put on our government apparatus by this is truly great, and by researching ways we can re-educate the people to speak a uniform language we can end this for good.
Centralize the Muscati Empire

The Muscati Empire is heavily decentralized, with the lands of Yemen and Qatar in particular enjoying great autonomy. By adopting Western methods of governance we will be able to centralize the state around a uniform center in Muscat, which will stregthen the Empire against any potential threats.
Restore Northern Rule

The Kingdoms of North Iberia have enjoyed independence ever since our forces were thrown out of Gaul in 997. This region is known since Roman times to be difficult to control, and indeed, the constant rebellions by the local populace rendered our hold in it practically non-existant even before the disaster in Gaul. This time, we will integrate the region properly, ending any notion of resistance against our rule.
Enact the Conversion Decree

A necessary step in securing our dominion would be to gain the loyalty of the population. The problem is that the Christian faith will always drive the people against us, no matter our policies towards them. Clearly, the Jizya system that guaranteed autonomy for the local Christians has outlived its usefullness, as the populace has adapted to it and no longer feels the need to convert. We will task the best scholars of Al-Andalus to design education programs that would spread the Arabic script as well as the Islamic faith among our subjects.
Down the African Coast

The Atlantic coast south of Morocco is a desolate desert, with no valuable resources and without any significant population. Its uselessness makes it particularly unattractive to other colonial powers. However, if someone was to take it, it would cut us off from the Sahel and Western Africa as a whole, so it's best that we lay claim to the region ourselves.
Reorganize Friesland

Liberal Prince Hinrich is doing terrible things in Friesland, upsetting the German nobilitiy and allowing Frisian nationalism to prosper. At this rate, he is going to be declaring complete independence from Brabant. We only need a good pretext to remove him.
Reconquer Friesland
We lost Friesland. This is a true catastrophe for Brabant, as a Friesland under enemy control is a terrible danger for our state. We must retake Frisia immediately.
Federalize Lower Saxony
Our influence in the Northwestern German states allows us to expand our deal with Westphalia and bring the entirety of Lower Saxony under our protection.
Integrate Frisia

Our past reorganizations of Frisia still left Friesland proper as a semi-independent state. We should end their eutonomy and directly incorporate the small nation, finally uniting the Lowlands in their entirety.
Unify Low Franconia

With the unification of the Low Countries, we have only one pressing matter left at hand - the Rhenish Germans. They still consider themselves different from us, refusing to fully integrate. It is an opportunity, however: since changing their mind and forcefully making them accept our customs is going to be incredibly expensive, we could instead recognize them as a different, albeit brotherly, nation - one that would be a constituent of a Low Franconian Union. Undoubtedly ambitious, this plan shall become the basis of the Flemish foreign policy, that may lead to something even greater.
Fate of the Martlet

Our cousins across the Channel, the English, have been suffering under the Danish yoke for half a millenium. When they finally decided to throw it off in 1797, their overzealousness caused an all-European emergency, the Martletist Wars, out of which we gained the duchies of Kent and Sussex. Now, the English are awakening once again. We understand their desires for freedom and we will support them, but perhaps they are a bit too... hotheaded. A more sensible, level-headed approach is needed. They will get their freedom, but as our subjects.
West Germanic Union

The Lowlands, England and Lower Saxony share many similarities, stemming from the same roots. Our search for security and stability in the region led us to gaining large swathes of land and the sympathy of the local peoples, who we may consider brotherly. Perhaps, its is Flanders' geopolitical destiny to end the separation between West Germanic peoples in the form of a new union - Westland.
Reclaim Daneland

Daneland was pried off of Denmark as a result of the Constantinople Accords, since Copenhagen completely failed to quell the Martlet Revolt by the English, and it had to be put down by the Gaels and the Brabanters. However, we find ourselves in a position to change that and reunite the Nordic peoples in their entirety!
Break the Peace of Caerlleon

The recent events on the Isles clearly signify that the Treaty of Caerlleon has outlived its usefulness. Changes in the political landscape require greater freedom of actions, and no matter the economic consequences, we shall renounce the Treaty and openly position ourselves against our former partner.
Invade the Midlands

With the Peace of Caerlleon broken, we can no longer be sure of our safety on the Isles. Our continuous prosperity requires immediate action: we shall invade the rich lands of York and Mercia, thus depriving our Southern neighbour of much of their powerbase.
Unify Prydain

We find ourselves at the brink of complete dominion over the entire isle of Prydain. Before us lay the heartlands of the Anglo-Saxons - Wessex and Lundenburg. It is time to finally bring an end to centuries of Germanic rule in the Isles and unify them under the true natives of these lands - the Celts!
Peace on the Isles

Gaeldom is triumphant. We have completely dominated the Isles, kicking out the Danes, the Anglo-Saxons and even the opportunistic Flemish kings. We do not, however, possess the means to alter the ethnic landscape of our newly-acquired land. In order to maintain a good public image, as well as to finally integrate the lands into the Union fully, we will have to come to terms with the inhabitants of these lands. Only then will the Isles truly know peace.
Ask for New Sjaelland

Our Danish allies have recently established a colony on the islands of New Sjaelland in the Pacific Ocean. Currently, this colony is more trouble than it's worth, as there are no immediate natural resources on the isles and the natives are hostile to all. As such, we believe that the Danes may be willing to part with these isles freely, instead giving them to us, who desperately need a colony to work with.
End the Southeastern Cession

The Southeastern Cession is the name of the part of England that was given to the King of Brabant in the aftermath of the Martletist Wars. We are unsure as to what the folks in Brussels have in mind regarding this land, and, besides, it was under rightful Danelander sovereignty since 1495 as the autonomous Duchies of Kent and Sussex. Currently, the Cession is the most immediate threat to stability on the isles, and it must be dealt with quickly.
Integrate the Free City

The Free City of Lundenburg was created in the aftermath of the Martletist Wars as both a compromise between the Danelanders and the Brabantians and an independent state of the Anglo-Saxons. As time passes, we can finally evaluate the results of this experiment - and they are not quite what we would have wanted. Lack of any sort of concrete legislation against Martletist thought turned the Free City into a hotbed of English separatism and otherwise negative dealings. Before this problem spirals out of control once again, we must end the Free City's independence.
Claim Britain

The Peace of Caerlleon ended as unexpectedly as it began. The Celts and us now look at each other with severe distrust, realising that war is an inevitability. Our move would be to lay claim on the traditionally English lands in the north as well as Wales, all of which hold valuable resources for our industry.
Unify Britain

In the Medieval times, Alba was heavily influenced by our Norse ancestors. Maybe not as much as Ireland, but we must nevertheless look to this example and prepare for a strike north, in an effort to disunite the Celts and end thir so-called 'Union'.
Integrate the Celts

After our successful unification of Great Britain, we find ourselves ruling over masses of Celtic peoples. Unfortuantely, we will have to accept that the Danelanders would remain a minority, and give equal rights to our new subjects. Cymru and Alba will now be integral parts of our Kingdom.
Turn off influence notifications
This decision allows you to turn off the influence change events. Be wary, however, that the minigame will decide your future expansion!
Turn on influence notifications
This decision allows you to turn on the influence change events.
End the Neapolitan Parliament

The city of Naples was left as an independent state following the succession crisis of the Hauteville Kingdom in 1823 and the collapse of their state. The local nobles, unwilling to take a side in the civil war, assembled a Parliament and declared the city and its surroundings to be neutral. With time, their politics began to be influenced by Martletists and the like, and we cannot let such an important city fall into Martletist hands, which, by extension, provides us a reason to occupy it.
Conquer Naples

The city of Naples was left as an independent state following the succession crisis of the Hauteville Kingdom in 1823 and the collapse of their state. The local nobles, unwilling to take a side in the civil war, assembled a Parliament and declared the city and its surroundings to be neutral. With time, their politics began to be influenced by Martletists and the like, and the threat of Martletist resurgence in the city provides us with a valid reason to occupy it.
Consolidate Longobardia

It was originally an ecclesiastic polity, but later shifted towards a more traditional secular power structure. While they are Shia and have no reason to cooperate with us outside of the current circumstances, we could convince them that the Hedjazi revolt is their last hope in the face of Wahhabi domination of the entire peninsula.
Incorporate Najran

The small Shia principality of Najran is a Yemeni polity established in the 17th century is the only remnant of the Zaydis. It was originally an ecclesiastic polity, but later shifted towards a more traditional secular power structure. It is the only other independent Yemeni state, and their subjugation will untie our hands in all foreign affairs.
Claim Yemeni Leadership

The Principality of Najran was established in the 17th century as an ecclesiastic polity, without any ambition to participate in Yemeni politics. However, the situation we find ourselves in presents a perfect opportunity to establish Shia rule over Yemen and bring peace to the land.
Move court to Sana'a
Governance would be more efficient if we moved our capital closer to the Yemeni heartland, allowing us to use the locals in the governing process and legitimizing our state.
Claim Hadhramaut

Hadhramaut is a region traditionally considered Yemeni that was forcefully deprived by the Muscati Empire. Discontent is frequent among the tribes, and many of them promise that if we were to lend them support, they would start an uprising in order to unite Yemen.
Claim Asir
Asir is a mountainous region to our north. The local tribes would welcome our rule if we employed the same methods tat we use when dealing with the southern tribes of Yemen.
End the Hadhramaut Governorate

The Hadhramaut Governorate was established in 1812 as a half-hearted attempt to keep the Yemeni tribes content with Muscati rule. It is now evident that the governorate has outlived its usefullness, as advancements in governance allow us to directly control the land. We shall seek further centralization if we want to modernize the country.
Authorise Missionary Efforts

Ibadi Islam is the faith of the Sultan and of the majority of the population in Muscat, but not outside of it. Large swathes of land, primarily in Hadhramaut and in the Persian Gulf do not follow Ibadism. Small-scale efforts to convert the locals have been made, but with centralization in full swing, we shall devote more attention to the matter.
Reconquer the Zanj Coast

We lost the Zanj Coast to the Geledi following their rapid rise after the fall of Ethiopia. Though our powerful navy protected Zanzibar, the mainland was under firm control of the Somali tribes. Circumstances have led to us regaining the main portion of our holdings, and we shall claim the rest of the coast in order to secure greated control over trade.
Hegemony over the East African Coast

Our glorious conquest of the Zanj Coast gave us dominion over many Swahili-speaking peoples. With them already holding considerable influence in out country, we might as well declare a complete integration of the Swahili and lay claim to all of their lands, including those held by Al-Andalus.
Form Sayhad

Muscat faces destruction at the hands of the Pan-Arabist movement. Our state is to be integrated into the larger Arab identity, and our people are to lose their unique worldview. But not all is lost: our dominant position in Southern Arabia opens an opportunity for the creation of a new identity. Sayhad was a region in modern-day Yemen appearing on some old maps, and its undefined nature allows us to shape it however we like, while maintaining the legitimacy of our new title. We shall adopt it as a defining state ideology.
Enforce Sayhadi Education

Building a national identity is not an easy thing. With many tribes abandoning their traditional nomadic lifestyle and settling down, we receive a large amount of children to educate in schools, which opens way for mass indoctrination. The state aesthetics will be formed accordingly, based on experience from the West, in order to spread the Sayhadi identity among adults.
Claim Bedouin Leadership
The deserts of Central Arabia are divided between two powers. We will mobilize the tribes and claim a dominant position among the Bedouins!
Claim Central Arabia

Central Arabia was dominated by the Wahhabi Emirate of Diriyah, until its demise at the hands of various rebels. The fall of this state created a power vacuum in Central Arabia, one which we are now powerful enough to fill.
Unite Central Arabia
Our control over Hedjaz, Hejd and Ha'il is now solidified. We shall create a new, centralized state and modernize the tribes, creating a synthesis of Islamic tradition and Western modernity.
North German League

The Bavarian-led German Confederation is clearly just a tool that Munich uses to cpread its influence and subjugate the German states. If we were to damage the international standing of Bavaria, we could convince the North German states to challenge the Southern dominance by creating a union of their own, with the first step towards a political federation being a break with Bavaria.
Create the Exarchate of Syria

The partisan war that the Syriac population had started against us brought untold destruction to the region of Syria, while also damaging our reputation worldwide and causing trouble on the homefront. Calls are heard from even the war hawks to stop the needless waste of resources and attempt to salvage what we can by granting Syria some autonomy.
Delineate the Sham Desert

Our tragic loss of Northern Sham made it so the desert to the east is no longer our sole domain that we don't have to worry about. The global trend of enroachment on yet unclaimed lands is obvious, and there is a good chance that Constantinople may become interested in the aformentioned desert in the coming future. We should offer the Greeks to prevent any potential border conflicts in advance by figuring out the borders in the desert.
Organize Mesopotamia

More than a thousand years after $COUNTRY_ADJ$ troops last sent foot in Mesopotamia, we have wrestled control of the region from the Muslims. But, just like before, it won't be easy to hold, as there is little to no loyal populace that we can rely on, with only small amounts of Assyrians present. It would be beneficial to immediately organize the region as an Exarchate and prepare to transfer governance to a loyal population base.
Create the Exarchate of Assyria

We have gained control of the Christian lands of Assyria. While there is substantial reasoning to be made in favor of granting it outright independence, the weakness that this state has shown most certainly push us towards instead organizing it as an Exarchate, so that the locals can have a significant say in the governance of these lands.
The Union of Bethlehem

The original idea of Michael Meshaka have become a subject of frequent debate in the Senate. As more and more lands comes under Imperial control in the Levant, the prospect of complete union with the local Christians comes closer, and the support for the idea starts coming from the locals themselves. An organized proposal by the Senate, The Union of Bethlehem, as it has been called, proposes the direct annexation of all Levantine exarchates and granting of rights to all Christians of these lands. Should it be realised, the Union will yield hundreds of thousands of new loyal subjects that the Empire can rely on.
Negotiate with Syria

Creation of the Syrian autonomy solidifed Christian influence in the whole of Egypt. The Majlis has been adjusted to fit disproportionally more Syriacs, as there are no other autonomous regions under Egypt. Such a situation heavily undermined the authority of the King, as the Christians have now wrestled control of the Majlis and can overrule his vetoes on legislations. The next step of the legal coup is negotiating the political reintegration of Syria, which will open way to getting rid of the decadent institution of the monarchy.
Union with Nubia

If one was to follow the flow of the Nile upwards, he would soon find himself in Nubia, a land starkly different from the civilized Egypt or Levant. Failure of the Nubian state to provide for its people, despite relative peace, left the area in a state that is more appropriate for the 18th century, with little advancement being made. For the betterment of the Nubian people, we will not deprive ourself of intervention and subsequent integration of Nubia into $COUNTRY$
Unite the Arabs

Disunity and strife plagued the Arab people since the end of the Islamic Golden Age. Invasions by Turks, Mongols, Habesha and Persians divided the Arabs, who would not form a state capable of challenging the invaders until recently. The era of disunity in the Middle East must end. We will unite the Arabs under a single state!
Invade Maghreb

Maghreb suffered greatly from the negligence of Qurtubah, who failed to prevent the Christians from gaining a foothold in the region despite massive advantages. The locals of the region clearly sympathize with us, so the restoration of Arab rule in Maghreb is only a matter of time.
Integrate Hedjaz
We no longer require the Hashemites to govern the Holy City of Mecca. We should revoke their mandate and install direct rule in Hedjaz.
Pacify Sham

The Sham, or Syria as it is known to the Christians, became a hotbed of resistance activity in a culmination of centuries of Muslim-Christian rivalry. People have died, wars have been fought and treaties have been signed, and yet Sham is still under Egyptian control, firm as it ever was. The resistance of the Syriacs lies broken, and the sympathies of the commoners are on our side - this chapter of our history can thus be considered complete, with the Battle for Syria ending with an Egyptian victory.
Seize the Holy Cities

Political developments in the Arabian peninsula make unfeasible our continued policy of non-intervention in local affairs. While we still have the opportunity, we should support the claim of some Hejazi nobles residing in our lands and claim the Holy Cities of Mecca and Medina for ourselves, making us a true spiritual leader of the Muslims.
Seize Rome

Our last attempt to return the Empire to Rome ended with the bloody War of the Verona Alliance, which lasted from 1632 to 1653 and ended in our defeat. This time, however, an opportunity to gain Rome peacefully presents itself: through some smart political machinations, a few bribes and promises that we do not intend to keep, we can gain control of the nvm i just realised this decision is compeltely useless
Unite the Midi

In the search for its destiny, the Arelat nation came at a logical conclusion - a herald of the Southern peoples, the liberator of the Midi and the guardian of the Alpes. It is not outward where the Arelat destiny lies, nor is it strictly inward, deeper into the ambitionless hole we were languishing in for so long. Arles' future lies among the fellow Southerners, in an eternal alliance of fraternity.
Restore Rule over Sicily

The stalemate between us and the Carlistas forced an unwanted truce in 1828. The island of Sicily fell firmly into enemy hands, and in the years that have passed, the island has been mismanaged to a terrible degree. We will have to deal with the  mess created, while also restoring the economic links between Africa and Sicily.
An Offensive into Africa
The Francescan invasion of Sicily has once again failed! We shall rally all Carlista loyalists and prepare to strike the enemy domains. The Hautevilles will be united!
Victory in Africa

Our victorious forces, just like Romans during the Punic Wars, have landed in Africa and completely defeated our foe. Francesco has reportedly fled to Arles, which means that Carlo is now the only Hauteville left standing. Despite the odds, we have prevailed!
Claim Tripolitania

For centuries, Tripolitania has been contested between us and the Muradid Sultanate, who enjoyed the support of Cordoba. The tug of war finally ended in the late 18th century, when the Muradids lost the last of their holdings around lake Djerid, and in 1830 they were pushed behind Wadi Zamzam. Their remnants, while having little to no actual forces do to so, still plot to retake their old domains. This petty rump state has to be destroyed.
Establish the Stato da Mar

Our domains encircle the Tyrrhenian Sea, and our navy is unrivaled in the Central Meditarranean. We dominate on the islands and on the continent, and it is only right that we reform the old dynastic state into the Dominion of the Sea, a true hegemon of the Meditarranean.
Claim Fezzan

Fezzan is an area to the south of Tripoli filled with important trade posts on the Trans-Saharan trade routes. The gradual subjugation of the region was started by the Muradids, but their decline in the 18th century made the region fall back into the nomads' hands. We will continue what was started.
Restore Ifriqiya

Before the vile Hautevilles, aided by the polytheists in Rome and beyond, took the city of Tunis in 1548, the area known to us as Ifriqiya was ruled by pious Muslims. Since this loss, the Maghreb never recovered, and in the next several centuries the Hautevilles slowly took over more and more land, despite military campaigns by our brothers in Qurtubah. But our spirit never faltered, and though our cause was thought to be done for, we have triumphantly returned to Tunis and reclaimed the glory of our ancestors that was lost so long ago!
Return to Tripoli

The city of Tripoli was contested between the Hautevilles and us in the 16th and 17th centuries, rapidly chaging hands until we finaly lost it in 1711. Many say that the loss of Tripoli spelled the end of the Muradid dynasty, as it was the last significant stronghold, surrounded by useless desert. But a miraculous military campaign allowed us to retake the city once more, meaning that the Muradid cause is not yet lost!
End the Geregistreerde

The institution of the Geregistreerde is slowing our industrial development and otherwise harming the society. Despite opposition from the Flemish aristocracy, we must give the peasants and the factory workers freedom to choose their place of work.
Colonize the Faruduan Interior

The jungles of Inner Faruduu are dominated by hills and mountains, all geologically part of the Guianan Shield. The steep slopes of the local mountains make it hard to access the many remote native villages in the area, but the abundance of rivers and rare specks of savannas make the settlement of the lands slightly easier. Many Faruduans have already began exploiting the area, and we should formalize the state's control over it.
Claim the Guinean Interior

The jungles and highlands of Guinea were, for the longest time, a land unfeasible for colonization and even exploration. Local tribes displayed no willingness for cooperation, frequently attacking our colonies. Though traversing the land is still a problem, we should use our right of Effective Occupation and incorporate the lands as a colony.
Prospect for Natural Resources

The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have created a need for large amounts of raw resources like iron and coal. Geologists of our country say that there may be some untapped deposits of valuable goods in our country's soil, and we could potentially exploit them through technological advancements.

Pacify Kurmanca

If one was to ask where Assyria ends and Kurmanca begins, he would be left with no answer, for the areas inhabited by the Assyrians and the Kurds roughly correspond with each other. Though they might have a lot in common, this exact circumstance of sharing the same batch of not-the-best land makes them mortal enemies. Clashes of faith defined the relationship of the two peoples since the Arab conquest, and the rise of the Yazidi faith in the 13th century only worsened the already complicated situation. Yazidi Sheikhs did little good to the Assyrian Church, upon which the Assyrian identity is based, and even under Turki rule the rivalry continued, culminating in the 1806 showdown between a newly-independent Assyria and the Kurdish tribes. Though Assyria subjugated the vast majotiry of them, a number were deemed too costly to subdue, residing around the lake Van, from where they plot to overthrow our state once again - and their plans must be taken care of.
Unite Mesopotamia

Beth Aramaye, or Asoristan, historically was an island of prosperity in a sea of war and strife, until the Mongol sack of Baghdad brought the area to the surrounding lands' standards. Though much improvement was seen during the Sakarman Empire, Mesopotamia still fell behind in development compared to the inner Iranian provinces due to the region being a constant battlefield between the Sakarman and the Ethiopian Empires. Turki efforts at courting the Assyrian people allowed a resurgence of the Christian culture in Lower Mesopotamia, but Assyria failed to gain hold of these lands upon independence in 1803. Under considerable pressure from the metropolitans of these lands, the Church of the East considers establishing control over the whole of Mesopotamia an utmost priority.
Subdue the Euphrates Bedouins

The southwestern shores of the Euphrates river and the desolate deserts surrounding it are inhabited by the Bedouin tribes, with small pockets of Christians concentrated in the coastal cities, most notably Deir ez-Zor. The Al-Uqaydat Confederation controls the important city, which, if it would be deprived of Egyptian support, would be easy to crush, giving us the control over both of the banks of the Euphrates.
Unite the Fertile Crescent

Centuries ago, before the Arab Conquest, the lands of Syria and Mesopotamia were united in their Christian faith and their Aramaic language. Though such a state of affairs was partially emulated during the Ethiopian rule, never since have the Aramaic people been a truly dominant force in the Middle East, ruling themselves under no foreign Empire, be it Ethiopian, Roman or Turki. The Land between the Rivers is now closer than ever to fulfilling the dream that was long sought after.
Union of the Aramaeans

Mesopotamia was thought to be truly lost to the Muslims, but the Assyrian state proved the doubters wrong, establishing a strong powerbase in the area. Now, the gaze of Beth Nahrain turns towards the west, across the Euphrates River, where our Aramaic brothers await liberation. They shall join our state, and the Aramaic world will be united!
Integrate Armenians

Armenian people are quite comparable to Assyrian: a relatively small group of Christians, stuck between a rock and a hard place of two, and recently even three, strong empires. Despite minor differences in faith, the historical circumstances in which our identities formed, as well as a long history of cohabitation allow the Armenian people to be effortlessly integrated into $COUNTRY_ADJ$ society.
Future of the Church of the East

The Church of the East split off from mainstream Christian Chruches in 424 due to theological disagreements regarding the nature of Christ. Isolated and persecuted, the Assyrian Church remained a hermit in the Christian world, being branded heretical by other Churches despite the fact that the original differences that caused the split were largely gone - the Nestorian doctrine was seen as more and more distant by the Assyrians, as they moved to the more conventional form of dyophysitism. Attempts to reconcile were made in the 16th century, which caused a schism in the Church of the East. But today, the Assyrian state is independent and is free to do as it wills. And the matter of Church of the East must thus be resolved once and for all.
Formalize Assyrian Governance

The Assyrian people historically organized around the Church of the East, which served as a formal goverment of the Assyrians as a 'state inside of a state'. This, combined with the lack of an actual independent Assyrian state, made the Patriarch of the East a practical political leader of the Assyrians. The 16th century schism in the Church of the East shook this institution, creating two rival lines of Patriarchs, one of which, the Shimun line, fled to Shiraz, while the other joined communion with the Coptic Church. The latter one enjoyed little support from the populace, and was destroyed following the seizure of Assyria by the Sakarman Empire in 1740. The Shimun Patriarchs were, as such, left as the only ones standing when the Sakarmans fell, becoming the leaders of an independent Assyria. But such a form of governance was never intended to be permanent - as the Patriarchal role is already heredital, assuming the title of the King of Assyria will give the country a more conventional intrnational position.
Found a $COUNTRY_ADJ$ University

Just like anywhere else in the world, education in Assyria was a thing for the rich and the smartest. Traditionally, the Church of the East served as the main source of learning, while an extremely small amount of the luckiest individuals studied abroad, most notably in Rome, Constantinople or Alexandria. The efforts of the Sakarman Shahs to court the Assyrians resulted in a massive development of Assyrian scholarship among the diaspora in Shiraz, and a significant amount of these learned men returned to Assyria upon its independence or in the years following. The modern Assyrian state, in order to meet the Western standards, needs a common education system to spread literacy among the commoners. Considering the multiethnic nature of our population, developing such a system would not be an easy task, but a local university would most certainly help us complete this task, along with a multitude of others.
Create a National Education System

In implementing universal education, Assyria faces problems that other states do not: its linguistic diversity. Unsurprisingly, it is quite hard to develop an education program that would suit all languages of Assyria, none mutually intelligible. However, some Social Scientists at the University of $CAPITAL$ say that this is not a problem, but rather is an objective circumstance that we must solve with the education reform. If the enforced education system was purposefully made monolingual, the fact that the national identities in most tribal peoples of the country are still not fully developed (compared to the European ones) could potentially force many people to think of themselves as Assyrians. Combined with the spread of Christianity among our non-Christian subjects, its could turn out to be a grand program that would change the cultural landscape of $COUNTRY$ forever.
Rescind Discriminatory Education

The consequences of our education reform turned out to be a little more fiery than we have expected. If we would have done this reform several decades earlier, there would certainly be less of those who called for an end to what they call 'cultural and linguistic genocide'. Their denouncements, both at internal and external levels, may just make the whole ordeal not worth it, if the calls grow too loud.
Assyrian Mesopotamia

The Mesopotamian heartland is now in Christian hands, for the first time in millenia. Thankfully, the Church of the East already had a vast ecclesiastical administration network in the area, so the complete integration of Mesopotamia, including its largest city of Baghdad, won't be a problem.
Restore Persian Caucasus

The links between the Christians of Persia and Assyria on one side and the Armenians on the other were strong during under Sakarman Empire, and could be traced back to Antiquity. In fact, in most Persian Empires there have been, Armenians constituted the majority of the Christian population. They were a link between the East and the West arguably more than the Assyrians, and they had great relations with the Church of the East. As the Caucasus was seized by Russia during the final years of the Sakarmans, we would have a valid casus belli to liberate the lands.
Accept the Iranians

Though our state has a Persian core, the many other Iranian people are still considered to be equal to a European or a Chinese person. All Iranian peoples shall be granted civil rights and integrated into Persia.
Intervene in Iran

Iran has been in flames for three decades already, but a nomadic onslaught on Shiraz, the capital of the fallen Sakarman Empire, marks a culmination of 37 years of civil war. In the light of the devastation that this invasion is expected to cause (the learned men of Shiraz are well-informed on the Mongol and Timurid invasions), the vast ecclesiastical system that the Church of the East had built among the many Assyrians and Persian Christians is under the yhreat of being completely destroyed. The fleeing Assyrians are proposing the unthinkable: Assyria should use its advanced military and, with Greek help, seize control of Iran. §RAn invasion will commence immediately, and we will need to be quick, lest the scope of our actions will be felt deeply.§!
Crown the King of Persia

Through fire and conquest, the Assyrian Army subdued the lands of Persia proper. Hundreds of thousands lay dead, the cities and the countryside are in rubble and the former nobility has been almost completely eliminated. The eastern provinces of the Church of the East remain as the only semblance of a functioning government in the devastated lands, as many join the congregation, seeing the feats that Assyria has acomplished, either in awe or fear. But in Nineveh, the political life is at its height: the Assyrians have never thought of such a possibility, but now they are in control of the whole of Persia! But the uncertainty of the future weighs down the celebrations. The Muslim resistance to occupation by the Christians has been high during the conquest itself, and now it is even higher - to survive and quell the brewing unrest, Assyria will need to fidn support among the locals it just conquered. With this in mind, the Patriarch called for an assembly of all of Persia, with the goal to elect and crown a new King.
Sword and Fire

The history Christianity in Persia was always coupled with persecution. The Sasanian Emperors executed thousands of the faithful, giving the Church a multitude of Saints and Martyrs. The Islamic conquest brought almost a complete end for Christianity: only the filthy Turki horse lords, in their stupidity, allowed the Assyrian Church to exist freely in Persia. Now, history has been avenged: Persia sits firmly in Christian hands. But we cannot wait for God to punish the heathens in the afterlife. §RThe pit of fire§! will await them in this life, unless they repent. Only then we may forgive their sins.
End the 'Sword and Fire' Policy

The policy of 'Sword and Fire' has seen great success in making the heathens of Persia see the light of Christ. However, the reaction from both the internal dissidents and the international community has been quite harsh. We are essentially close to being an international pariah because of the methods we employ. It would be wise to accept what we got out of the policy and end it for now.
Collect Tribute

The complete collapse of trade links in the former lands of the Sakarman Empire led to an economic downturn in all for all its former subjects, with the Kurds being no exception. The underdeveloped highlands did not allow the tribal leadership to acquire any source of income other than the traditional taxation, and so, all in Kurdistan took up the questionable practice of forcing tribute out of the locals, like a herder would periodically cut a sheep's wool.
Rein in the Tribes

The traditional tribal organization of the Kurds allows for much autonomy for a considerable part of the population, which includes the tribes that are only nominally subject to whoever would attempt to subjugate a considerable amount of them. This is the reason why the Kurds would rarely constitute something even remotely close to a singular, united polity that would act as one - a tribe bows to no one but its leader, and there are only so many tribes one person can control directly, having to instead rely on subordinate chiefs. But the Shekh's rule must be absolute if Kurdistan is to advance, both politically and socially.
Consolidate Lake Van

The populous shores of the Lake Van, thanks to their remoteness and practical uselessness for neighboring powers, have remained unconquered even by the Sakarmans, whose rule was only nominal in these lands. The brave Kurdish tribes kept it to themselves for centuries, vying for power among each other while fighting off the fools that attempted to challenge the Kurdish independence. But change is felt in Kurdistan - technological advancements in various fields allow enemy armies to more effectively penetrate into the mountains, with the Assyrian Expedition of the Greek Army conducted in 1806 showing that an advanced enough force can easily break the Kurdish resistance. The independent tribes must for once unite under a single banner, to descend from their mountain fortresses as a united force that will assert itself as a modern polity in the Middle East.
Unite Kurdistan

Characterized by rough terrain and a fierce population, Kurdistan was never truly conquered by any powers outside of it. The social organization of the Kurds, being at the same time a political one, allowed the Kurdish polities to lie dormant under foreign yoke. It first came to light when the Mongol Ilkhanate collapsed in 1290 due to internal strife - the Yazidi Shekhdom survived the 'conquest' and came out of it stronger, managing to sway many Turks roaming Western Anatolia at the time. This was Kurdistan's highest point of political advancement - but the Yazidi Empire fell it the 1430s, with the tribes being once again set adrift. Strife and oppression were the only things the Kurds had known since then - and time has come for the Kurds to reclaim their rightful place in history, unified for the first time in centuries.
Second Kurdish Uprising

In 1799, following a coup by the Pashtuns and the Qizilbash, the Sakarman Empire fell into a decades-lasting civil war. Already severely overextended after their conquest of the Middle East from Ethiopia, the Sakarman forces quickly retreated out of Syria, and then Northern Mesopotamia, where the reigns of power were taken by the Assyrians. The Kurdish tribes did not sit idly and watch tribes fall into Assyrian hands one by one, launching an uprising that came close to dismantling the newly founded Assyrian state - only to be stopped in their tracks in 1806 by the Greek Army, that was sent here in an expedition, albeit deeply unpopular one, to help the Assyrians. In the decades that followed, we witnessed an unprecedented growth of Assyrian power under the lazy protection of Constantinople. And though repeating our feats in the First Uprising might seem like an impossibility now, the odds of a direct Greek intervention would be non-existant if we took the required precautionary measures - perhaps, 1806 could be avenged?
The Eastern Tribes

The Kurdish society is, unfortunately, divided among two different religions - Sunni Islam and Yazidism, as well as a small minority of Shias. Though our ways of life and political situation are similar enough for a common identity to be somewhat felt, rarely did the majority Sunni Kurds of the east care about the affairs of their Yazidi brothers in the west. Such a division was also partially caused by a great difference in geographic circustances - the Western Kurds had their mountain to hide in, while the Eastern Kurds were too nestled too deep inside the urbanized Persians, a significant amount even populating the urban centers. Independence was thus left to be enjoyed only by the Western Kurds, whose duty it is now to unite all Kurds and set foot in lands that had not seen Kurdish rule for centuries - the rich Lower Mesopotamia.
A Caucasian Bulwark

Relations between the Kurds and the Caucasian peoples have, just like any other relations in the region, a long and troubling history. The Kurds technically occupy a part of the Armenian homeland, and the Armenians know and despise it, though the newly-founded Armenian state never attempted to penetrate into the mountains with their limited resources. The Azeris, on the other hand, were quite friendly towards the Kurds, thanks not only to the shared Iranian heritage, but also to a respect of each others' faiths. With the Kurds emerging triumphant in their struggle with the Assyrians, we can deal a final blow to the Armenians and incorporate the Azeris, thus securing our northern flank.

Subdue the Deserts

The deserts of Central Asia are harsh and inhospitable for permanent settlements. Only nomads and rare merchants can be seen in these lands. But these locations are of strategic importance to us, and must thus be tamed.
Unite the Caucasus

The Caucasian lands are diverse, situated on a crossroads of large empires and sparsely populated - all of this lead to long periods of foreign domination. But circumstances have led the Caucasus to regain the reins of power: the Bagrationis of Georgia strenghtened their state, the Atabekians of Armenia headed a heroic fight against the Iranians, the peoples of the Northern Caucasus fended off the Russians and the Azeris overthrew the tyrants in Shiraz. The Caucasus is witnessing a historic moment: the complete unification of the land.
Caucasian Unity

The Caucasus is about roughly divided between the Muslims and the Christians, whose relations are strained by hundreds of years of rivalry. We need to create an administration capable of accepting all religions.
Add Assyrians to the Caucasus

The Assyrians, though not usually considered to be part of the Caucasian peoples, technically inhabit a portion of the Caucasus Mountains, and have historically intermingled with the other Caucasian peoples. Considering they are our brothers in faith, they could be integrated with little problem.
Add Kurds to the Caucasus

The Kurds, though not usually considered to be part of the Caucasian peoples, technically inhabit a portion of the Caucasus Mountains, and have historically intermingled with the other Caucasian peoples. Considering they are our brothers in faith, they could be integrated with little problem.
Claim Greater Epirus

The Armanite Project, started in the late 18th century, which unified the various disorganized Latin-speaking and Illyrian-speaking peoples of Epirus, has come so far that a national identity is now unbreakable. The Armanite State, as such, may no longer focus on internal issues and must go on the offensive to unite with the Armanites of Greece.
Proclaim the Neapolitan Republic

Offensive in Syria
Syria is in flames: not even the Army can safely reside in the region. In no province of the Empire should such horrors be allowed. We must decide on a course of action.
Institutionalize the Melkites

The Melkites are a friend of ours in our process of integrating Syria. Thanks to our funding, each year their influence on the Syrian population increases, and many of them hold administrative positions in local governments. To fully integrate Syria we must go further, and merge the Melkites with the state by making them into the local bureaucracy, as well as ensuring their representation in the Legislative.
Incorporate Dayru z-Zawr

Dayru z-Zawr, or Ed-Deir for short, was placed under control of the local Bedouin tribes after the fall of the Sakarmans. The remoteness of the city, which stands in the middle of the Syrian Desert, as well as its location on the edge of three powers (Assyria, Egypt and Iran) made it quite problematic to control, so the Egyptian King eventually offered the Bedouins vassalage, which they accepted. The so-called Uqaydat Confederation is weak, though, and their lands are better be confiscated as per the recent reforms in land ownership.
Support Dhofari Independence

Dhofar was ceded by Bilarab al-Harthi, Sultan of Mascat, to a nobleman from the Jaboub clan. This nobleman turned out to be extremely selfish and willing to sell out his domain and turn against anybody in exchange for wealth. As such, if we wish to gain a foothold in South Arabia, we could exploit this and help Dhofar win the fight against Muscat.
Reinstate the Alexandria Greek School

The Alexandria Greek School was famous throughout the Eastern Mediterranean during the times of Ethiopian rule for being the important link between the European and Coptic scientific communities. Unfortunately, it was forced to close down during Muhsin I's Siege of Alexandria. Though the scholars that worked in the School heavily contributed to the creation of the Egyptian parliamentary system at the Treaty of Alexandria, the School was never re-opened. Perhaps it would be beneficial to contact Constantinople and attempt to restore it.
